Let
\[
S=\sqrt{x^2+400}+\sqrt{y^2+900}+\sqrt{(x-40)^2+(y-50)^2}.
\]
First, by the triangle inequality,
\[
\sqrt{x^2+400}+\sqrt{(x-40)^2+(y-50)^2}
\ge \sqrt{(x+40-x)^2+(20+50-y)^2}
=\sqrt{40^2+(70-y)^2},
\]
so
\[
S\ge \sqrt{40^2+(70-y)^2}+\sqrt{y^2+30^2}.
\]
Now interpret the right-hand side as
\[
DQ+QE
\]
where \(Q=(0,y)\), \(D=(40,70)\), \(E=(30,0)\). Since \(Q\) lies on the \(y\)-axis, reflect \(E\) across the \(y\)-axis to \(E'=(-30,0)\). Then
\[
DQ+QE \ge DE'=\sqrt{(40+30)^2+(70-0)^2}=70\sqrt2,
\]
with equality when \(Q\) is the intersection of the line \(E'D\) with the \(y\)-axis. The line through \((-30,0)\) and \((40,70)\) has slope \(1\), so it is \(y=x+30\); hence at \(x=0\), \(y=30\).

So the minimum can occur only when \(y=30\), and then equality in the first triangle inequality requires
\[
(x,20)\ \text{and}\ (40-x,20)
\]
to be positively proportional, which gives \(x=20\).

Therefore the minimum value is attained at
\[
(x,y)=(20,30),
\]
and
\[
S_{\min}=\sqrt{20^2+20^2}+\sqrt{30^2+30^2}+\sqrt{20^2+20^2}
=20\sqrt2+30\sqrt2+20\sqrt2=70\sqrt2.
\]
Also, \(0\le 20\le 40\) and \(0\le 30\le 50\), so this point satisfies the domain constraints.

In the first quadrant the other three inequalities are automatic once \(x,y\ge0\), so the feasible set there is just
\[
0\le x\le a,\qquad 0\le y\le b,\qquad ax+by\le \frac{a^2+b^2}{2}.
\]
If \(a\ge b\) (\(k\ge1\)), this line meets \(y=b\) at \(x=\frac{a^2-b^2}{2a}\in[0,a]\) and meets \(x=a\) below the rectangle, so each forbidden corner is a triangle of area
\[
\frac12\cdot \frac{b^2}{a}\cdot \frac{a^2-b^2}{2b}=\frac{b(a^2-b^2)}{4a}.
\]
Subtracting all four such triangles from the rectangle gives
\[
[\text{good area}]=4ab-4\cdot \frac{b(a^2-b^2)}{4a}
=4ab-\frac{b(a^2-b^2)}{a}
=\frac{2b^2}{\,}\!,
\]
so
\[
P=\frac{[\text{good area}]}{4ab}=\frac{b}{2a}=\frac1{2k}.
\]
By symmetry, if \(0<k\le1\) (i.e. \(a\le b\)), we get
\[
P=\frac{a}{2b}=\frac{k}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{
P(k)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{k}{2}, & 0<k\le1,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{1}{2k}, & k\ge1,
\end{cases}
}
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
\boxed{P(k)=\frac12\min\!\left(k,\frac1k\right).}
\]
This gives \(P(1)=\tfrac12\), and \(P\to0\) as \(k\to0\) or \(k\to\infty\), as expected.
